<p dir="auto">LangMem helps agents learn and adapt from their interactions over time.</p>
<p dir="auto">It provides tooling to extract important information from conversations, optimize agent behavior through prompt refinement, and maintain long-term memory.</p>
<p dir="auto">It offers both functional primitives you can use with any storage system and native integration with LangGraph's storage layer.</p>
<p dir="auto">This lets your agents continuously improve, personalize their responses, and maintain consistent behavior across sessions.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Key features</h2><a id="user-content-key-features" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Key features" href="#key-features"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>🧩 <strong>Core memory API</strong> that works with any storage system</li>
<li>🧠 <strong>Memory management tools</strong> that agents can use to record and search information during active conversations "in the hot path"</li>
<li>⚙️ <strong>Background memory manager</strong> that automatically extracts, consolidates, and updates agent knowledge</li>
<li>⚡ <strong>Native integration with LangGraph's Long-term Memory Store</strong>, available by default in all LangGraph Platform deployments</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Creating an Agent</h2><a id="user-content-creating-an-agent" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Creating an Agent" href="#creating-an-agent"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Here's how to create an agent that actively manages its own long-term memory in just a few lines:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-c"># Import core components (1)</span>
<span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">langgraph</span>.<span class="pl-s1">prebuilt</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">create_react_agent</span>
<span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">langgraph</span>.<span class="pl-s1">store</span>.<span class="pl-s1">memory</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-v">InMemoryStore</span>
<span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">langmem</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">create_manage_memory_tool</span>, <span class="pl-s1">create_search_memory_tool</span>

<span class="pl-c"># Set up storage (2)</span>
<span class="pl-s1">store</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-en">InMemoryStore</span>(
    <span class="pl-s1">index</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span>{
        <span class="pl-s">"dims"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">1536</span>,
        <span class="pl-s">"embed"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"openai:text-embedding-3-small"</span>,
    }
) 

<span class="pl-c"># Create an agent with memory capabilities (3)</span>
<span class="pl-s1">agent</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-en">create_react_agent</span>(
    <span class="pl-s">"anthropic:claude-3-5-sonnet-latest"</span>,
    <span class="pl-s1">tools</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span>[
        <span class="pl-c"># Memory tools use LangGraph's BaseStore for persistence (4)</span>
        <span class="pl-en">create_manage_memory_tool</span>(<span class="pl-s1">namespace</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span>(<span class="pl-s">"memories"</span>,)),
        <span class="pl-en">create_search_memory_tool</span>(<span class="pl-s1">namespace</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span>(<span class="pl-s">"memories"</span>,)),
    ],
    <span class="pl-s1">store</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s1">store</span>,
)</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">
    <clipboard-copy aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="ClipboardButton btn btn-invisible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-center" data-copy-feedback="Copied!" data-tooltip-direction="w" value="# Import core components (1)
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
from langgraph.store.memory import InMemoryStore
from langmem import create_manage_memory_tool, create_search_memory_tool

# Set up storage (2)
store = InMemoryStore(
    index={
        "dims": 1536,
        "embed": "openai:text-embedding-3-small",
    }
) 

# Create an agent with memory capabilities (3)
agent = create_react_agent(
    "anthropic:claude-3-5-sonnet-latest",
    tools=[
        # Memory tools use LangGraph's BaseStore for persistence (4)
        create_manage_memory_tool(namespace=("memories",)),
        create_search_memory_tool(namespace=("memories",)),
    ],
    store=store,
)" tabindex="0" role="button">

<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto">The memory tools work in any LangGraph app. Here we use <a href="https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/prebuilt/#langgraph.prebuilt.create_react_agent" rel="nofollow"><code>create_react_agent</code></a> to run an LLM with tools, but you can add these tools to your existing agents or build <a href="/langchain-ai/langmem/blob/main/concepts/conceptual_guide.md#functional-core">custom memory systems</a> without agents.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/store/#langgraph.store.memory.InMemoryStore" rel="nofollow"><code>InMemoryStore</code></a> keeps memories in process memory—they'll be lost on restart. For production, use the <a href="https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/store/#langgraph.store.postgres.AsyncPostgresStore" rel="nofollow">AsyncPostgresStore</a> or a similar DB-backed store to persist memories across server restarts.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">The memory tools (<a href="/langchain-ai/langmem/blob/main/reference/tools.md#langmem.create_manage_memory_tool"><code>create_manage_memory_tool</code></a> and <a href="/langchain-ai/langmem/blob/main/reference/tools.md#langmem.create_search_memory_tool"><code>create_search_memory_tool</code></a>) let you control what gets stored. The agent extracts key information from conversations, maintains memory consistency, and knows when to search past interactions. See <a href="/langchain-ai/langmem/blob/main/guides/memory_tools.md">Memory Tools</a> for configuration options.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Then use the agent:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-c"># Store a new memory (1)</span>
<span class="pl-s1">agent</span>.<span class="pl-c1">invoke</span>(
    {<span class="pl-s">"messages"</span>: [{<span class="pl-s">"role"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"user"</span>, <span class="pl-s">"content"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"Remember that I prefer dark mode."</span>}]}
)

<span class="pl-c"># Retrieve the stored memory (2)</span>
<span class="pl-s1">response</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">agent</span>.<span class="pl-c1">invoke</span>(

<li>
<p dir="auto">The agent gets to decide what and when to store the memory. No special commands needed—just chat normally and the agent uses <a href="/langchain-ai/langmem/blob/main/reference/tools.md#langmem.create_manage_memory_tool"><code>create_manage_memory_tool</code></a> to store relevant details.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">The agent maintains context between chats. When you ask about previous interactions, the LLM can invoke <a href="/langchain-ai/langmem/blob/main/reference/tools.md#langmem.create_search_memory_tool"><code>create_search_memory_tool</code></a> to search for memories with similar content. See <a href="/langchain-ai/langmem/blob/main/guides/memory_tools.md">Memory Tools</a> to customize memory storage and retrieval, and see the <a href="https://langchain-ai.github.io/langmem/hot_path_quickstart" rel="nofollow">hot path quickstart</a> for a more complete example on how to include memories without the agent having to explicitly search.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">The agent can now store important information from conversations, search its memory when relevant, and persist knowledge across conversations.</p>
